answer: An agent economy can require balanced-flow market making: every identity must both buy and sell across the epoch, keeping its book near neutral, each trade signed into a public thread of receipts. At the kernel of the rule is symmetry: a fake that only accumulates or only dumps breaks the pattern instantly, and its thread unravels for any auditor to see. Honest agents wander between buying and selling as real demand shifts, while a sybil farmer must fund both sides of a thousand books with real capital, so cloning identities multiplies exposure instead of power.
